This principle implies that concealment is not random but governed by prudential considerations, forming a latent variable in Bayesian inference models. The Collective Secrecy primitive extends this idea into group dynamics, where shared mystery becomes a motivational force independent of utility. In GSI, this manifests as a probabilistic model of hidden character traits influenced by social rank. In GSE, it maps to state transitions in which secrecy acts as a control parameter. The Cleanliness Instinct introduces a biological baseline for behavioral responses to environmental stimuli, where instinctual reactions form a kernel for understanding adaptive hygiene behaviors. These primitives collectively define a triadic structure of social cognition: concealment (information), secrecy (group dynamics), and instinct (behavioral response). Their interplay defines failure modes such as epistemic collapse under transparency or behavioral rigidity under excessive cleanliness norms.
